title: Universal filtration truncations and their distinguished triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with localizations taken in a common larger universe. Let $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ be the localization of bounded-below cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. Finite means that $F^aM=M$ and $F^{b+1}M=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, independently of cochain degree. This localization has the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] induced by filtered mapping cones. Forgetting the filtration $\omega:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ and each graded-piece functor $\operatorname{gr}^p:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ are exact.

For every integer $r$, the subcomplex truncation $t_{\ge r}M=F^rM$ and quotient truncation $t_{<r}M=M/F^rM$, with induced and quotient filtrations, descend to exact functors. They have graded pieces respectively $\operatorname{gr}^pM$ for $p\ge r$ and $p<r$, and zero otherwise. Write $DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $DF^{+,<r}$ for the full subcategories whose graded pieces vanish for $p<r$ and $p\ge r$, respectively. There is a natural distinguished triangle $t_{\ge r}M\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}}M\xrightarrow{q_{r,M}}t_{<r}M\to(t_{\ge r}M)[1]$, induced by the subcomplex inclusion and quotient. It is uniquely determined, up to unique isomorphism inducing the identity on $M$, among distinguished triangles $L\to M\to R\to L[1]$ with $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$.

For $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Hom}(L,t_{\ge r}M)\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}\circ -}\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(t_{<r}M,R)\xrightarrow{-\circ q_{r,M}}\operatorname{Hom}(M,R)$ are bijective, naturally in their arguments. Thus $t_{\ge r}$ is right adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,\ge r}$, and $t_{<r}$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,<r}$.

Put $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$. This functor has only the graded piece $\operatorname{gr}^pM$, and $\omega T_p=\operatorname{gr}^p$ canonically and naturally. On the full subcategory with all other graded pieces zero, the truncation maps identify $T_p$ with the identity, and forgetting filtration is an equivalence to $D^+(\mathcal C)$, inverse to placing a complex in filtration degree $p$. All assertions use vanishing in the derived category, so apply even when the other graded complexes are acyclic rather than literally zero.
